definitions.explanation: acting primarily out of self-interest, always considering personal gain in decisions

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{打算的|ださんてき}な{人|ひと}だ。
{打算的|ださんてき}な{考|かんが}え{方|かた}はやめなさい。
examples.english: Stop thinking in such a self-serving way.

examples.japanese: {打算的|ださんてき}な{付|つ}き{合|あ}いは{長続|ながつづ}きしない。
examples.english: Relationships based on calculated self-interest don't last.

notes:
WORD FORMATION:
- {打算|ださん} (calculation, self-interest)
- {的|てき} (suffix making adjectives)

NUANCE:
Always used with negative connotation, describing someone who constantly weighs benefits and costs in relationships and decisions, prioritizing personal gain over genuine feelings or principles.

CONTRAST:
- {打算的|ださんてき} (calculating, self-interested)
- {純粋|じゅんすい} (pure, sincere)
- {無欲|むよく} (selfless, unselfish)

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
- {損得勘定|そんとくかんじょう} (calculating profit and loss)
